text:
alex: FYI customer on rwd3-64k is seeing a spike of 429s during nightly ingest bursts. started at ~00:10 UTC, ~200 req/s for a couple minutes then 5xx/429 mix. they say requests are fairly identical except context length varies a lot.

jen_support: thanks alex. can you paste a minimal repro (curl + headers) and the top-line error? is it 429 or 429 + some body like "rate limit model RPM exceeded"?

alex: error body is `{"error":"rate limit exceeded","detail":"per-model rpm/ppm quota"}` from the API. curl we gave them:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd3-64k","prompt":"<large payload...>","max_tokens":150,"stream":false}'
```

requests are fired from a worker pool: 40 workers, each does sequential >1 call per second during ingest window. so effective client concurrency ~40, short bursts to 200rpm for that model.

maria_prod: important detail: are they using embeddings + generation or only generation? and are they using multi-turn with KV-cache pinned? longer contexts count more toward TPM (token-per-minute) so that could explain throttling.

alex: only generation. avg input length ~3k tokens for that run (they concat logs). at peak we see `429` on ~30% of requests, others 200, some 502/504 when backend falls back.

rate-limiter-bot: policy event: per-model rate policy triggered for `rwd3-64k` -> metric=RPM limit (75 req/min per-customer-model) scope=customer-acct-10234. token budget alert: TPM threshold exceeded.

jen_support: OK that helps. looks like two factors: (1) per-model RPM ceiling (requests/min) and (2) TPM accounting because large contexts. our platform enforces both. the documented defaults are not public in-thread, but ops can check exact quotas.

tom_sre: a few immediate checks: 1) confirm whether requests are batched by the client; 2) inspect `x-request-id` on failed responses to correlate; 3) check if they hit `max_concurrency` for that model variant (we have per-variant concurrency slots).

alex: they do no client-side batching. i attached the failed response headers (copied):

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
x-rate-limit-model: "rwd3-64k: 75rpm"
x-request-id: "req_9a8b7c"
x-server-time: "2026-08-12T00:11:23Z"
```

jen_support: nice. can you ask them to try these repro steps: 1) reduce number of parallel workers to 8 and keep same per-worker throughput; 2) add exponential backoff (start 200ms, *2, jitter); 3) if they need sustained throughput, switch to dedicated capacity / reserved plan for that model. mention that long context raises TPM quickly so they may hit token budget ceiling even if RPM is fine.

maria_prod: also useful: suggest they swap to a cheaper variant (rwd3-64k-lite or rwd3-32k) for bulk ingest — quantized variants have higher concurrency headroom and lower per-token accounting in some profiles. we can also temporarily bump their per-model quota for troubleshooting.

alex: customer tried lowering concurrency to 10 — 429 rate dropped to ~5% and most errors disappeared. they want to understand thresholds: can we provide the exact per-model numbers (RPM/TPM/concurrency) for their acct?

tom_sre: i can pull the live policy for acct-10234. typically defaults are 75rpm, 150k tpm for large-ext models, concurrency 20 for rwd3-64k on hosted tier. but these are configurable per-account. i'll open a quick audit and post exact values.

rate-limiter-bot: policy snapshot for acct-10234: {"rwd3-64k":{"rpm":"75","tpm":"150000","concurrency":"20"}}

jen_support: when you respond to the customer, include: - their policy numbers, - suggested mitigations (reduce concurrency, add retry/backoff, fall back to smaller model variant for high-token jobs, consider dedicated), - short-term workaround (spread requests using a leaky-bucket client or per-second pacing).

alex: will do. adding note: they also saw auth 401 for a handful of requests during the burst window — likely transient token handshake failures when platform overloaded. should we flag as SRE review?

tom_sre: yep if 5xx/401s spike with rate events we should correlate infra CPU/GPU metrics. i'll check scheduler queue length and autoscale events for that time window. if backend pods exhausted file descriptors or kernel queues, that can amplify errors.

maria_prod: one more tip to share with customer: when context lengths vary a lot, measure token distribution and set client-side token-based pacing (e.g., target <= X tokens/sec) instead of pure requests/sec. that prevents TPM storms.

alex: thanks all — i'll send a summary to the customer with the numbers and the repro patches. tagging @tom_sre for follow-up and audit logs. :thumbsup:

tom_sre: got it — i'll post results from infra check in this thread tomorrow.

jen_support: thanks team, good triage.
